gen-dafont-pixel-operator-fs-epilogue: Epilogue curves loosely, with tall-bodied lowercase and short stubby ascenders drawn in a single wire-like line that never tightens up. Pixel Operator is the rigid one, fixed-width and terminal-flavored; Epilogue is the one that flows.
gen-dafont-prime-fs-nunito: Prime hangs its bulky lowercase from the line like clothespins, with strokes that shift in weight without ever lurching. Nunito follows with big round bowls and terminals that stop well short of the stem, which softens the whole thing.
gen-dafont-prime-general-sans: General Sans keeps its pressure steady from first letter to last, with an x-height that fills the line and smooth curves. Prime, with its closed letters and gentle swings in stroke weight, sits above it at a slightly larger size.
gen-dafont-radikal-fs-epilogue: Radikal leads with wire-bent s curves that never thin at the spine, and tall lowercase bodies spaced with generous room. Epilogue loosens things up beneath it, curvy and open, with stubby ascender tips and a monoline skeleton that feels unclamped.
gen-dafont-radikal-fs-nunito: Radikal holds its s curves full all the way through the bend. Nunito's big round bowls and terminals that finish clear of the stem leave the lowercase feeling open where Radikal's letters feel closed.
gen-dafont-radikal-general-sans: Smooth, unobstructed curves and an x-height that fills the line give General Sans a steady, confident read from start to finish. Radikal's closed, wire-bent letters make the sharper statement against its open ones.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-asap: Asap reads as open arcs in its c, with a body height that nearly matches the capitals, so the line feels full and clear. Rounded Elegance, set so tightly its letters almost overlap, gives warmth, while Asap supplies the steady reading.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-epilogue: Rounded Elegance sets its characters so close they almost overlap, with wide entrances into each letter and a monoline build. Epilogue shares that single-line construction, adding tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips that make the match feel natural.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-quicksand: Quicksand builds tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs, with terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Rounded Elegance shares its monoline build, so a long passage would read as one smooth, gentle voice.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-general-sans: General Sans reads smoothly, its curves unobstructed and its x-height filling the line. Both fonts share a similar monoline build, and that kinship is the strongest thing about the pair, with Rounded Elegance adding closeness and warmth.
